detail.body:
FIX #63414, where the bug is:
Serving nvidia/Nemotron-3.5-Parse with --compilation-config.compile_mm_encoder true kills
the engine on the first image request, and the server stops answering entirely
(Connection refused afterwards — it is a fatal EngineDeadError, not a per-request 500):

```
AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'cu_seqlens'
  vllm/model_executor/models/radio.py:501 in forward   (under torch._dynamo.aot_compile)
EngineCore encountered a fatal error -> **EngineDeadError**

```
## Purpose of this PR

`--compilation-config.compile_mm_encoder true` does nothing for RADIO. Since the encoder
was rewritten to standalone modules (#58468), `RadioLayer` carries no
`@support_torch_compile`, so the flag is silently a no-op for `Nemotron-3.5-Parse`,
`Nemotron-Parse-2.0` and `nano_nemotron_vl` — the encoder is never compiled and nothing
says so.

Simply decorating the layer does not work either. Three independent static-shape
assumptions are in the way, each only visible once the previous one is fixed:

1. **Wrong dynamic dim.** RADIO packs NaViT tokens into dim 1, so marking dim 0 (the
   value inherited from InternVL before the refactor) bakes the packed length.
2. **Varlen metadata is unaddressable.** `dynamic_arg_dims` keys by argument name, and
   `cu_seqlens` was wrapped in the `MaskMetadata` dataclass, so its length could not be
   marked dynamic. It now travels as tensor arguments.
3. **Traced vs runtime mismatch.** `mask_meta` was built only when more than one image
   was present. Encoder profiling uses 2 items, so tracing saw an object while real
   single-image requests passed `None`. A no-guards graph keeps whichever form it traced
   and drops the other **silently** — measured below. When the layer is compiled, every
   call now carries metadata: one image gives `cu_seqlens [0, n]` (unmasked attention
   over a single sequence), and a uniform `[B, n, C]` batch is packed the way the conv3d
   video path already did.

Two things that review caught and this PR now does deliberately:

- **Packing only happens when the layer is compiled.** TORCH_SDPA does not synthesise
  `cu_seqlens` the way the FlashAttention and Triton wrappers do — handed a packed
  sequence it splits it and runs one attention call per item. Always packing cost a
  uniform batch B calls per layer instead of one (B=8, 2 layers: 16 `apply_sdpa` calls
  vs 2, bit-identical output), plus a `.tolist()` host sync per layer; a 128-frame video
  chunk would be 128 launches per layer. A consistent `cu_seqlens` form is only required
  for the no-guards graph, so uncompiled the batch stays unpacked and the default path is
  unchanged from main.
- **Only dim 1 is marked dynamic.** Every path reaching the compiled layer packs to
  `[1, total, C]`, and torch specializes a size-1 dim to 1 even when it is marked
  dynamic, so listing dim 0 bought nothing and implied a batch dim that cannot vary.
  Correctness rests on the batch-1 invariant, which is now asserted once in
  `RadioVisionEncoder.forward` so an unpacked caller fails on a clear precondition
  instead of a size/stride assert deep inside inductor.

Building the metadata must not copy host memory: `torch.tensor(list, device=cuda)` is a
blocking host sync on every encoder forward, which `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error` rejects.
Uniform batches use a device-side `arange`; the variable-length helper stages through
pinned memory.

`RadioVisionEncoder.forward` keeps its `MaskMetadata`-facing signature and unpacks once,
so `nemotron_parse3_5` and `nano_nemotron_vl` need no changes.

## Test Plan

Dedicated 1-GPU H100 jobs, one per variant, image built from `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly`
(`0.33.0rc1.dev229`, torch `2.14.0+cu130`) with the refactored RADIO files overlaid from
main, so the stock arm is exactly upstream and the only difference between images is this
PR. Each image verifies its own `radio.py` sha before running. Nemotron-3.5-Parse, 3
document images, greedy, four arms per variant covering both ViT attention backends.

## Test Result

Adding the SPDA check for this

```
stock (main)   RadioLayer decorated: False
  off      FLASH_ATTN  requests OK | alive | RadioLayer compile mentions 0 | errors 0
  on       FLASH_ATTN  requests OK | alive | RadioLayer compile mentions 0 | errors 0
  sdpa_off TORCH_SDPA  requests OK | alive | RadioLayer compile mentions 0 | errors 0
  sdpa_on  TORCH_SDPA  requests OK | alive | RadioLayer compile mentions 0 | errors 0

this PR        RadioLayer decorated: True
  off      FLASH_ATTN  requests OK | alive | compile mentions 0  | errors 0
  on       FLASH_ATTN  requests OK | alive | compile mentions 85 | errors 0
  sdpa_off TORCH_SDPA  requests OK | alive | compile mentions 0  | errors 0
  sdpa_on  TORCH_SDPA  requests OK | alive | compile mentions 85 | errors 0
             (both compiled arms run with VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error)
```

The flag is a no-op on main — 0 compile mentions with it on, on either backend. With this
PR the encoder really compiles:

```
RadioLayer] Compiling a graph for compile range (1, 2147483647) takes 2.21 s
RadioLayer] Dynamo bytecode transform time: 0.33 s
```

**No behaviour change with the flag off, on either backend** — served text is
byte-identical to main:

```
off       stock=4bb7b431 9ff45c59 ab96d7f8   PR=4bb7b431 9ff45c59 ab96d7f8   3/3
sdpa_off  stock=4bb7b431 3cac4d5d a3c3f497   PR=4bb7b431 3cac4d5d a3c3f497   3/3
```

The silently-dropped-mask failure in point 3 is measured, not inferred. On a compiled
layer (reference spread `max|masked - unmasked| = 0.5742`):

```
traced with a cu_seqlens tensor, then called with None:
  AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'size'
traced with None, then called with a cu_seqlens tensor:
  max|out - correct| = 0.5742   max|out - traced-form| = 0.0469  -> mask silently dropped
```

Packing a uniform batch is bit-exact on the FlashAttention wrapper, which flattens the
batch and synthesises this very `cu_seqlens` when it is omitted:

```
attn backend: FLASH_ATTN
B=4 n=30: max|unpacked - packed+cu_seqlens| = 0.000e+00   (control, one big sequence: 0.9404)
B=8 n=64: max|unpacked - packed+cu_seqlens| = 0.000e+00   (control: 0.8105)
B=2 n=97: max|unpacked - packed+cu_seqlens| = 0.000e+00   (control: 0.3828)
```

On TORCH_SDPA it is not free, which is why packing is gated on the layer being compiled:

```
compile_mm_encoder=False -> pack_uniform_batches=False | apply_sdpa calls = 2   (same as main)
compile_mm_encoder=True  -> pack_uniform_batches=True  | apply_sdpa calls = 16  (opt-in only)
```

On the size-1 dim, checked with `error_on_recompile` (a plain `torch.compile` recompiles
silently and hides this), torch 2.14.0: marking `[0, 1]` and marking `[1]` specialize
dim 0 identically, so dim 0 was inert.

### Performance

Dedicated pod, all arms on the same GPU, interleaved round-robin, 4 rounds, 64 distinct
DocVQA pages per experiment. 

For the page/s and TTFT at c = 16, we see some performance gain. This PR fix the issue without impacting anything and brings performance gain in some cases

| metric | stock off | this PR off | this PR on | A/A noise floor |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| TTFT p50 @ c=1 | 286.1 ms | 285.1 (-0.4%) | 287.3 (+0.4%) | 5.10% |
| TPOT p50 @ c=1 | 1.655 ms | 1.632 (-1.3%) | 1.635 (-1.2%) | 6.42% |
| pages/s @ c=16 | 5.892 | 6.209 (+5.4%) | 6.323 (+7.3%) | 2.83% |
| TTFT p50 @ c=16 | 2338.9 ms | 2200.0 (-5.9%) | 2149.7 (-8.1%) | 8.77% |


### Coverage

Also validated on **Nemotron-Parse-2.0** and **nano_nemotron_vl**
(NVIDIA-Nemotron-Nano-12B-v2-VL-BF16, B=13/B=32 tiles): with the flag off this PR is
byte-identical to main on both, and an in-situ probe inside the live model shows the
encoder output is bit-exact between the packed and unpacked paths
(`max|packed-unpacked| = 0.000000e+00`).

## Behaviour note

Enabling the flag changes the output for some pages. The first difference is always a
bounding-box coordinate of ~0.001 normalised (1-2 px), but under greedy decoding that can
rewrite the rest of a long generation, so similarity ranges from 1.000 to 0.43 by page.
This is **torch.compile on the encoder, not the varlen path**: with the flag off this PR
is byte-identical to main on all three models and on both attention backends, and
`cu_seqlens [0, n]` for one image is bit-exact against unmasked attention. Flagging it
since the flag is opt-in.

inline_comments.body:
🔴 Every RADIO encoder layer now gets an empty weight prefix. Quantization ignore lists and per-layer FP8 encoder-attention scales stop matching for Parse 2.0, Parse 3.5 and nano_nemotron_vl. The new `@ support_torch_compile` wrapper takes `prefix` as a keyword. It forwards `prefix` only if the wrapped `__init__` declares it, and `RadioVisionEncoderLayer.__init__(self, *args, **kwargs)` does not. Fix: have `RadioVisionEncoderLayer.__init__` take `prefix` (and the other named args) explicitly and pass them to super, or drop the redundant decoration, so `{prefix}.layers.{i}` reaches `InternVisionEncoderLayer`.

<details>
<summary>Why this was flagged</summary>

`InternVisionEncoder` builds each layer with `prefix=f"{prefix}.layers.{layer_idx}"` (intern_vit.py:351). The new decorator on `RadioVisionEncoderLayer` (radio.py:482) wraps its `__init__(self, *args, **kwargs)`. `_support_torch_compile.__init__` (decorators.py:377, 401) binds `prefix` itself and forwards it only when `"prefix" in sig.parameters`. That check is False for `*args, **kwargs`, so the prefix is silently dropped. On the base branch the undecorated subclass passed `prefix` through `**kwargs`, so the names were correct. One trigger is FP8 encoder attention with `mm_encoder_fp8_scale_path`. There, `MMEncoderAttention.layer_name` (mm_encoder_attention.py:340) is the same for all layers, and the scale lookup at :481 raises "FP8 attention enabled but scales not found for layer". The decorator's "support decorating multiple times" guard (decorators.py:360) does not help here. It only checks direct `__bases__`, and `TorchCompileWithNoGuardsWrapper` is a base of the parent, not of this class.

**Verification:** The wrapper forwards `prefix` only `if "prefix" in sig.parameters` (decorators.py:401-402), which is False for `RadioVisionEncoderLayer.__init__(self, *args, **kwargs)` (radio.py:482-492). On the base commit the Radio class was undecorated, so `prefix` passed through `**kwargs` and was forwarded correctly. This is a regression.

</details>

inline_comments.body:
Confirmed by measurement, and fixed. On a compiled layer (reference spread
`max|masked - unmasked| = 0.5742`):

```
traced with a cu_seqlens tensor, then called with None:
  AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'size'

traced with None, then called with a cu_seqlens tensor:
  max|out - correct| = 0.5742   max|out - traced-form| = 0.0469
  -> the graph keeps the form it traced and the mask is silently dropped
```

So the mixed case is a silent wrong answer, not just a crash. `RadioModel.forward` now
carries varlen metadata on every call: dynamic resolution builds it unconditionally, and
a uniform `[B, n, C]` batch is packed into `[1, B*n, C]` the way the conv3d video branch
already did. Packing is free on the attention path these models use — the wrappers
flatten the batch and synthesise exactly that `cu_seqlens` when it is omitted:

```
attn backend: FLASH_ATTN
B=4 n=30: max|unpacked - packed+cu_seqlens| = 0.000e+00   (control, one big sequence: 0.9404)
B=8 n=64: max|unpacked - packed+cu_seqlens| = 0.000e+00   (control: 0.8105)
B=2 n=97: max|unpacked - packed+cu_seqlens| = 0.000e+00   (control: 0.3828)
```

The earlier `prefix` finding no longer applies: it was about
`RadioVisionEncoderLayer.__init__(*args, **kwargs)`, which #58468 removed. The new
`RadioLayer.__init__` already declares named arguments including `prefix`.

issue_comments.body:
One remaining issue: `RadioVisionEncoderLayer` is now decorated twice (its own `@support_torch_compile` plus the inherited one on `InternVisionEncoderLayer`), so `TorchCompileWithNoGuardsWrapper.__init__` runs twice per layer. Each run registers a bytecode hook, and the second one overwrites `_bytecode_hook_handle`, so the first hook can never be removed. `cleanup()` on engine deletion drops only the last one, and Dynamo's hook table keeps the layer alive.

With an in-process engine (`VLLM_ENABLE_V1_MULTIPROCESSING=0`) and `compile_mm_encoder` on, Nemotron Parse 3.5 keeps all 27 RADIO layers and ~947 MiB on the GPU after `del llm` (33 MiB on main). The static path (Parse 2.0, fixed-tile `nano_nemotron_vl`) is affected too, and it did not leak before.

A two-line fix in `vllm/compilation/wrapper.py`:

    if envs.VLLM_USE_BYTECODE_HOOK and mode != CompilationMode.STOCK_TORCH_COMPILE:
        # A decorated subclass of a decorated class runs this init twice.
        self.cleanup()
        self._bytecode_hook_handle = (...)

Plus a regression test: decorate `A` and a subclass `B(A)` with `@support_torch_compile`, construct `B`, call `cleanup()`, `del`, `gc.collect()`, and assert a weakref to it is `None`. It fails without the line.

**On current main the flag is a silent no-op for RADIO, not a crash.** `RadioLayer`
carries no `@support_torch_compile`, so `compile_mm_encoder` never compiles the encoder
and nothing reports that. The original `AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no
attribute 'cu_seqlens'` from #63414 no longer reproduces; the three underlying
static-shape obstacles still do, once the layer is decorated.

Re-validated on two dedicated 1-GPU H100 jobs, image built from
`vllm/vllm-openai:nightly` with the refactored RADIO files overlaid from main, so the
stock arm is exactly upstream and the only difference between images is this PR. Each
image verifies its own `radio.py` sha before running.

```
stock (main)   RadioLayer decorated: False
  flag off : requests OK | engine alive | RadioLayer compile mentions 0 | errors 0
  flag on  : requests OK | engine alive | RadioLayer compile mentions 0 | errors 0

this PR        RadioLayer decorated: True
  flag off : requests OK | engine alive | compile mentions 0  | errors 0
  flag on  : requests OK | engine alive | compile mentions 85 | errors 0
             (both PR arms under VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error)

RadioLayer] Compiling a graph for compile range (1, 2147483647) takes 2.21 s
```

With the flag off the served text is byte-identical to main (`4bb7b431 / 9ff45c59 /
ab96d7f8`, 3/3). Also checked on Nemotron-Parse-2.0 and nano_nemotron_vl: flag-off
byte-identical, and an in-situ probe shows the encoder output is bit-exact between the
packed and unpacked paths (`max|packed-unpacked| = 0.000000e+00`).

Performance: no measurable change. All arms on one GPU, interleaved round-robin, 4
rounds, 64 distinct DocVQA pages per arm so the encoder runs on every request.

| metric | stock off | PR off | PR on | A/A floor |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| TTFT p50 @c1 | 286.1 ms | -0.4% | +0.4% | 5.10% |
| TPOT @c1 | 1.655 ms | -1.3% | -1.2% | 6.42% |
| pages/s @c16 | 5.892 | +5.4% | +7.3% | 2.83% |
| TTFT p50 @c16 | 2338.9 ms | -5.9% | -8.1% | 8.77% |

Every delta is at or below the A/A floor (stock vs stock through the same harness); the
flag-off arm is bit-identical computation to main, so its apparent gains are noise and
set the empirical floor.

One sync bug was found by that E2E and is fixed here: building `cu_seqlens` with
`torch.tensor(python_list, device=cuda)` is a blocking host copy on every encoder
forward, rejected by `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error`. Uniform batches now use a device-side
`arange`; the variable-length helper stages through pinned memory.

## Claude Code Review

This pull request is from a fork — automated review is disabled. A repository maintainer can comment `@claude review` to run a one-time review.

**Additional findings** (outside the current diff — GitHub can't attach inline comments there):

- 🟣 `vllm/model_executor/models/radio.py` — Pre-existing, left by a partial fix: nano_nemotron_vl users with compile_mm_encoder can still crash, or get images attending across each other. RadioModel.forward passes mask_meta=None for a single image or when imgs_sizes is absent (radio.py:653). It passes a tensor when there are several images. The compiled layer has no guards, so it keeps whichever form it traced first. Fix: give the compiled RadioVisionEncoderLayer the same cu_seqlens form on every call. Build the mask metadata unconditionally in RadioModel.forward whenever tokens are packed (any imgs_sizes, including one image), as this PR does in RadioWithNeck.

  <details><summary>Why this was flagged</summary>

  RadioModel.forward (radio.py:649-656) builds mask_meta only `if imgs_sizes is not None and len(imgs_sizes) > 1`. nano_nemotron_vl.py:1106 calls it with imgs_sizes for dynamic-resolution images, and nano_nemotron_vl.py:1140 calls it with no imgs_sizes for non-conv3d video chunks. So RadioVisionEncoderLayer gets cu_seqlens=None on some calls and a tensor on others. TorchCompileWithNoGuardsWrapper drops all guards (vllm/compilation/wrapper.py:137-146). Whether cu_seqlens was None at trace time is therefore baked into the graph. If profiling traced with several images, a later single-image request fails like the AttributeError in #63414. If it traced with None, later multi-image batches silently run unmasked attention across images. With this PR the layer finally gets past the dim-1 and cu_seqlens-length shape asserts for these models, so this None-ness mismatch is now the failure they hit. The PR fixes it only for nemotron_parse3_5's RadioWithNeck.

  **Verification:** radio.py:637-656 `RadioInternVisionModel.forward` still sets `mask_meta = None` and only builds it under `if imgs_sizes is not None and len(imgs_sizes) > 1`. After the first compile, calls go to `TorchCompileWithNoGuardsWrapper.__call__` (decorators.py:615-620) with no guard-driven recompile. So the layer gets a tensor on some calls and None on others.

  </details>

<!-- bhrv:f6a43bedef01ed12 -->

Rebase looks right: `RadioLayer` is the correct target now, prefix is declared, and the three-shape analysis in the commit message checks out against the decorator (dims keyed by arg name, guards dropped, 2-item profiling). Two inline notes with concrete failing cases. Also the PR body still describes `RadioVisionEncoderLayer` subclassing InternViT and lists a unit test that was removed; the commit message is current, the body is not.

Review was AI-assisted (Claude); I checked the findings before posting.

Both items addressed, thanks. Dim 1 only plus the batch-1 assert is the right shape, and gating the pack on `do_not_compile` keeps flag-off identical to main. Two nits, take or leave: the gate could also skip `_inter_image_mask_metadata` for a single image, since TORCH_SDPA still does one `.tolist()` sync per layer there with the flag off; and the new block in `RadioModel.__init__` splits the `summary_idxs` comment. LGTM otherwise. @DarkLight1337 this needs the `ready` label for pre-commit to run.
